remaining.what: returnAfterPause starts any return whose break begins in a week an earlier return re-planned from that week’s startBeforeReturn, with no check that it reports the same break. A separate, later break restarts from the state before the first break: after a 16-day break and its re-entry (1x5 @RIR4), a 5-day break brings back 3x5 @RIR3 at the pre-break known load and a 70-75 minute long run; the return steps and the run RETURN mode are lost.
remaining.origin: Same-week variant present since R7A1-FREEZE-A1 (its C5 rule); cross-week variant introduced by the A2 fix of QE-R7A1-03. Not on R7A-FREEZE-2.

notReadyRecord.blocker: QE-R7A1-09 (HIGH) and QE-R7A1-10 (MEDIUM) from the engineering re-check, D59 (blocking) from the SSCTR re-check; QE-R7A-01 and D53 stay open through them
notReadyRecord.rootCause: The return’s starting point is read from week-boundary snapshots, not from the break itself. Return supersession (C5) has no break identity: "a newer report of a break" is implemented as "any return whose break begins in a week an earlier return re-planned" (startBeforeReturn) and "any slot already eased" (the easy-slot text), so a separate later break is read as a correction of the earlier one. And the state a return starts from is the start of the pause week (stateTrace[pauseWeek]), so what the athlete executed in that week before the break is lost.
